concerns: Consider refactoring generic IllegalArgumentException in controllers/services to custom domain exceptions to improve API error handling.
Using constructor injection with @Autowired is completely functional but redundant in modern Spring Boot versions.
The frontend uses simulated local state for onboarding instead of making real fetch requests to the backend API.
Some components could be further modularized to reduce the footprint of App.svelte as more dashboard features are added.
Thread.sleep in PauseEnforcerImpl runs synchronously, which could block execution threads in production unless executed asynchronously.
Using an injectable java.time.Clock instead of calling OffsetDateTime.now() directly in the service would make the time-dependent query test cases more robust.
Having the entire onboarding, modals, filters, and accounts pool layout inside App.svelte makes the component monolithic and less maintainable.
The onboarding flow and accounts list rely entirely on local state mocks and should be integrated with real API fetch requests to the backend.
